To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
learning styles and learning patterns do not significantly affect students’ learning performance in the WebCT-based MIS graduate course.

the following variables did not have any significant impact on learning performance: (a) gender, (b) age, (c) job status, (d) ethnicity, (e) year of admission, (f) previous Web-based learning experience, (g) MIS preparation, and (h) WebCT learning patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of learning styles, learning patters, and other selected background factors on learning performance in WebCT online learning.
the impact of student factors on their learning performances in a WebCT online course.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at the MIS graduate level, students’ learning performance is not affected by their different learning styles (i.e., visual, auditory, or tactile), WebCT learning patterns (i.e., reading, listening, or writing), and other selected background factors (i.e., gender, age, year of admission to the MIS program, previous Web-based course learning experiences, and job status), except their ethnic groups (i.e., Asian, African, or European American).
the students in the MIS graduate course were able to learn equally effectively in a WebCT course regardless of their learning styles, learning pattern, and background.
the WebCT online learning system can be used as an effective tool for teaching graduate MIS courses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WebCT online learning environment is a good environment for graduate MIS students to learn.
the Web-based learning environment is a good fit for all students.
the WebCT-based MIS graduate course has been a great success in terms of students’ learning performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the students who were more successful in this online MIS course were the ones who had a high degree of comfort with computers, had a strong interest in learning, and were willing to spend a lot of time on the course.
students are not learning equally well in a WebCT course, and that learning styles and learning patterns do have an impact on learning performance.
learning styles are not the most important factor for learning in a WebCT environment.
